newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power prices hold mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power prices hold mostly steady.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Friday with many traders looking to clinch next week contracts rather than doing Monday only business, industry sources said.
"There isn't a whole lot of weather, so people have been looking to take care of the week rather than doing just Monday," said one Mid-West power marketer.

Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Monday peak, non-firm power prices were talked steady to higher at $19.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $18.00-21.00 on Thursday for Friday business, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak Monday non-firm MAPP power was said to be steady at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Monday were talked higher at $19.00-22.00 from $17.00-19.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak Monday power was said to be unchanged at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.
MAIN peak power for the five business days of next week was said to have traded at $21.00 per MWh, although the trade was not confirmed.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Monday were reported to be steady to higher at $17.00-19.00 from $16.50-18.50 on Thursday, the sources said.

In ECAR, Consumers Power Co said it was investigating the cause of a shutdown at its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power plant in Michigan and had not yet set a date for the plant to resume electricity production.
The plant was shut Thursday after a problem with electrical equipment at a main generator.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was notionally assessed higher at $22.40-22.90 from $22.00-22.50 on Thursday, the sources said.
Peak ECAR power for the five business days of next week was said to have traded at $17.50 in the south and at $23.00 in the north, although the trades were not confirmed.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Monday delivery were assessed steady at $14.00-16.00 in the south and $19.00-21.00 in the north, the sources said.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were pegged steady at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.
February SPP was said to be steady at $22.00-23.00, while March peak SPP was assessed steady at $20.50-20.85 per MWh.
